lines.text: Rome. The new emperor, Vespasian, needs money. A great deal of it.
I guessed: a fine for peeing in the street. Wrong!
Pee was useful. Laundries washed wool with it.
So Vespasian put a tax on it.
So the emperor held a coin under his nose. Does it smell?
No. Yet it comes from pee.
That is why: money. And in Paris, street urinals were later named after him: vespasiennes.
lines.say: That is why: money. And in Paris, street urinals were later named after him: vespa-zyenns.
